a1.say: Let's solve Can You Attend Every Meeting?, using the Sort plus Neighbour Check approach.

a1.cap: Given meeting times [start, end], return true if one person can attend all of them (a meeting may start exactly when another ends).
a1.say: Given meeting times start, end, return true if one person can attend all of them (a meeting may start exactly when another ends).

lines: Given meeting times [start, end], return true if one person can attend all of them (a meeting may start exactly when another ends).

a1.cap: For example, with meetings = [[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]], the answer is false.
a1.say: For example, with meetings equals 0, 30, 5, 10, 15, 20, the answer is false.

a1.cap: Sort by start time. Any conflict must be between neighbours, so check that each meeting starts no earlier than the previous one ends.
Let's walk through it with meetings = [[9,10],[1,3],[4,8],[7,9]].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with meetings equals 9, 10, 1, 3, 4, 8, 7, 9.

a1.cap: Time complexity is O(n log n) and extra space is O(1) extra.
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n log n and extra space is O of one extra.

a1.cap: That's the Sort + Neighbour Check approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
